report_name: LockBit, INC_RANSOM, KRYBIT Claim New Ransomware Victims

threat_actors.name: LockBit
threat_actors.description: Notorious ransomware group that claimed an attack against City International Hospital in Vietnam as part of a wave of attacks on November 19, 2026.

threat_actors.name: DireWolf
threat_actors.description: Ransomware group that claimed an attack against CobbleStone Software as part of a wave of attacks on November 19, 2026.

threat_actors.name: KRYBIT
threat_actors.description: Ransomware group that claimed an attack against Alumil S.A. as part of a wave of attacks on November 19, 2026.

threat_actors.name: INC_RANSOM
threat_actors.description: Ransomware group that claimed an attack against Centered Co., Ltd. as part of a wave of attacks on November 19, 2026.

threat_actors.name: SETTRA
threat_actors.description: Ransomware group that claimed attacks against Albuquerque Plumbing, Heating & Cooling, Biokinetics and Associates, and Crystal Springs Resort as part of a wave of attacks on November 19, 2026.

threat_actors.name: HYFLOCK
threat_actors.description: Ransomware group that claimed attacks against Africapital Management and Alberto Álvarez as part of a wave of attacks on November 19, 2026.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: All mentioned ransomware groups use a ransomware payload to encrypt files on the victim's network, causing operational disruption and supporting financial extortion.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The ransomware groups steal sensitive data and upload it to their own servers before encryption, threatening to leak it publicly if the ransom is not paid (double extortion).

attack_patterns.name: Financial Theft
attack_patterns.description: The overarching tactic for all mentioned groups is financial extortion, leveraging data encryption and the threat of data leakage to pressure victims into payment.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware actors were suggested to attempt to delete shadow copies using tools like vssadmin.exe to hinder recovery efforts.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 5e8a3b1c-4d7e-4f6a-9a2b-1c9d8e7f6a5b
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-20
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    - Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    - OriginalFileName: 'VSSADMIN.EXE'
  selection_cli:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'delete shadows'
      - 'Delete ShadowStorage'
      - 'Resize ShadowStorage'
  condition: 1 of selection_img and selection_cli
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity, though rare.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor activity mentioned as a hunting hint.
